findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_recent_transactions, get_sync_status · Private data: get_address_approvals, get_address_exposure, get_address_risk, get_recent_transactions, get_wallet_graph_walk · Public sink: get_address_compliance.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_recent_transactions, get_sync_status · Private data: get_address_approvals, get_address_exposure, get_address_risk, get_recent_transactions, get_wallet_graph_walk · Public sink: get_address_compliance

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_address_compliance" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
